newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs not to tap state oil reserves after blast.
newsitem.headline: Czechs not to tap state oil reserves after blast.

text.p: The main Czech crude oil refiner, Ceska Rafinerska a.s., said on Saturday that it would not be necessary to tap state crude reserves after an explosion which closed its refinery operations at Litvinov earlier in the day.

In a statement, spokesman Ales Soukup said a meeting of Ceska Rafinerska officials, along with officials from parent firm Unipetrol a.s., petrol distributors Cepro a.s. and Benzina a.s. and the Industry and Trade Ministry had determined that supplies "will be adequate for the short-term".
It said the decision was made after a reveiw of supplies at Cepro and Benzina and supplies at Litvinov's sister refinery at Kralupy.

The blaze broke out just past midnight in a pumping station after an explosion of undetermined origin. At one point it directly threatened eight petrol tanks holding more than 10,000 tonnes of petrol.

The fire was brough under control later in the day, but the Litvinov refinery in the northeastern part of the country had to be shut indefinitely. Production is to be stepped up at the at the Kralupy refinery, north of Prague.
